target_customer: Business people and semi technical users who understand web basics but are not professional developers and want to build web apps
problem: Building a web application required coding skills or a contractor. Appcubator offered drag and drop creation and hosting of Django apps with downloadable code.
business_model: Freemium SaaS: free basic use, 35 dollars per month for custom domain and support, and team built sites from a flat 480 dollars

founders.name: Karan Sikka
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the TechCrunch and YC launch posts (September 2013).

founders.name: Ilter Canberk
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder. The page says he later worked on Spectacles at Snap.

competitors.name: dockPHP
competitors.what: Hosted app building service similar to Appcubator

technical_complexity.rationale: A visual builder that generates and hosts standard Django code with a database, logins and themes is substantial but uses known web frameworks.

defensibility.rationale: Code export removed lock in, and competitors like Bubble offered similar builders.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not shown in sources. The company went inactive and the domain is now for sale.

market_need_then: Non developers wanted to prototype web apps without hiring contractors, and TechCrunch noted several similar services already existed. No demand figures were found.

branding.name_origin: Likely a play on app and incubator, but no source says so
branding.domain_note: Exact appcubator.com, which is now a domain for sale page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and practical (the easiest way to prototype web applications)

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, the YC blog and Webrazzi in September 2013; no community found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is confusable with AppIncubator and similar names and no brand coverage beyond launch posts was found.

outcome_analysis: Appcubator launched publicly in September 2013 as a drag and drop Django app builder in a category that already had Bubble and dockPHP. No source reports funding, a shutdown notice, an acquisition or a pivot, so the cause of inactivity is not public. The one failure factor listed is an inference from the crowded category and is not stated by the founders.
notes: No funding information was found in searches (VCBacked has a profile without amounts; CB Insights results were for AppIncubator, an unrelated company). The standard YC deal is not recorded as a round. The cause of inactivity is not public. The site appcubator.com is a domain for sale page.
